title: Choose LinkGuard's visual world
question: The roll assigned Return to Sender. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll. Sketches show the new full-page block screen.

options.label: Return to Sender
options.lineage: Post office return slips, franking stamps and parcel address labels
options.thesis: A link is an address; LinkGuard is the sorting office that stamps the bad ones and ticks the reason on the slip.
options.viewport: Kraft band across the top with the shield mark; a white address label shows where the link really goes; a tilted red stamp reads NOT SAFE; a 'reason for return' slip ticks plain-language reasons; one big Go back button.
options.risk: Turns into a nostalgic post-office costume if the stamp and paper go beyond the signature slip and the header band.

raised.raise: One stamp form at every scale: the in-page badge, popup row, click warning and block page all use the same stamp, from 14px to 120px.
Colour commits whole regions: the kraft band owns the shell and the white label owns the content, with no tints or gradients in between.
A hard line budget: the slip shows at most three reasons in everyday words; anything more sits behind 'More details'.
Three inks per surface plus the state colour, with every rule a single hairline.
One decision fills the block screen: Go back is under the thumb and on Enter, and everything else is quieter.
State is carried by form as well as colour: suspicious gets a dashed outline and one stamp border, dangerous a solid double rule and a filled stamp.

options.label: Weather Warning
options.lineage: National weather-service yellow / amber / red warnings
options.thesis: Every link gets a warning level with what to do about it, like the weather forecast.
options.viewport: A full-width band in the level's colour with 'Red warning: take action', an impact-by-likelihood grid placing this link, and 'What you should do' in three plain lines.
options.risk: Familiar: yellow/amber/red is where most safety UIs land, so it is clear but not distinctive.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.viewport: A giant pixel headline over dense columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: non-technical people don't identify with type specimens, and pixel lettering slows a warning down.
options.risk: Reads as a design object, not a safety tool.
options.kept: One form repeated at many sizes.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.lineage: Illustrated zoo and garden guide maps
options.thesis: Sites as lobes of colour on a map.
options.viewport: A green headland lobe holding the link.
options.case: Loses both axes: the playful tone undercuts a stop, and a map doesn't explain a link.
options.kept: Flat colour that commits to whole regions.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.viewport: A folded card listing the reasons.
options.case: Loses both axes: handwriting reads informal, the opposite of the trust a block screen needs.
options.risk: Charming but not believable as protection.
options.kept: A hard budget: the sides must not overflow the tape.

options.label: Centre-Rail Edition
options.thesis: Reasons as apparatus in the margin.
options.viewport: Twin text columns around a rail of keys.
options.case: Loses both axes: scholarly density is the opposite of a two-second read.
options.risk: Too much to read under stress.
options.kept: One-pixel ruling discipline and three inks.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One warning owns the whole screen.
options.viewport: Full-bleed site preview, actions down the right rail.
options.case: Holds focus but loses identity: a feed suggests swiping on, the opposite of stopping.
options.risk: Feels like content, not a stop.
options.kept: One thing owns the viewport; the next action is one gesture away.

options.label: Emission Lines
options.thesis: Risk as hairline lines on a charcoal rail.
options.viewport: A rail of ticks with the link blooming above.
options.case: Loses both axes: abstract and dark-lab, so non-technical people won't read it as a warning.
options.risk: Beautiful and illegible to the audience.
options.kept: State carried by line form, not hue alone.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What security apps ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Navy header with a shield, a red 'Threat blocked' card, Go back / Proceed.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every antivirus product by design.
